assumptions: E is a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable space and canonical volume, including dimension zero. alpha,beta are NNReal, 0<alpha<=beta. U or V is genuinely C2; actual Hessian at every point and direction lies between alpha*norm(v)^2 and beta*norm(v)^2.

Every Gibbs law is the actual volume.tilted(-potential). Probability, finite second moments, score integrability, centered score pairing and covariance bounds are derived. No minimizer, finite input moments, partition constant, derivative/score/covariance or well-behaved certificate is supplied.
units.statement: The actual Gibbs mu=volume.tilted(-U) is probability and id belongs to L2(mu). For every direction v, covarianceBilin(mu)(v,v)>=norm(v)^2/beta. This is the linear-observable covariance corollary of Cramer-Rao, not the full nonlinear-observable theorem or a matrix-inverse result.

steps.title: Derive actual Gibbs probability and score second moment
steps.text: The existing canonical Gibbs gradient theorem derives the positive integrable exponential weight and actual score-square integrability from C2 Hessian bounds, using genuine weighted domination and full-space score integration by parts. Reuse that producer, without supplying a probability or moment certificate.

steps.title: Derive position L2 without a minimizer
steps.text: Strong gradient monotonicity between zero and x gives alpha norm(x)<=norm(gradient U(x))+norm(gradient U(0)). Square this and dominate by the integrable score square plus a constant under the actual probability law. Thus id is genuinely L2 and its Bochner mean exists. Zero norm is handled separately.

steps.title: Prove centered linear-score pairing with all IBP products integrable
steps.text: For a unit direction v put p=E_mu X, q(x)=inner(x-p,v), a(x)=DU(x)[v]. Actual position and score L2 imply q, a, qa are integrable as required. The full-space integration-by-parts API is applied only after deriving the weighted q, weight times derivative q, and derivative weight times q integrability. Since Dq[v]=1 and D(exp(-U))[v]=-exp(-U)a, normalize by the true positive Z_U to obtain E_mu qa=1. No mean-score-zero hypothesis is needed.
steps.formula: \mathbb E_\mu[q a]=1,\quad q=\langle X-\mathbb EX,v\rangle,\quad a=DU(X)[v],\quad\|v\|=1.

steps.title: Bound the actual directional score second moment
steps.text: The existing genuine score IBP identifies the weighted score square with the actual Hessian directional integral. The upper Hessian beta bound and probability normalization give E_mu a^2<=beta. All score-square, Hessian and product integrability are proved before integral algebra.

steps.title: Integrate an actual nonnegative square
steps.text: Expand the integrable nonnegative square (a-beta q)^2. Combining E qa=1 with E a^2<=beta yields beta^2 E q^2>=beta. Positivity of beta follows from 0<alpha<=beta, so divide to get variance>=1/beta. Actual covarianceBilin is identified with the centered q square using proved id L2.

steps.title: Scale every direction and include dimension zero
steps.text: Handle v=0 directly. For v nonzero use u=v/norm(v), apply the unit-direction result and use the true covariance bilinear map scaling. This quantifies all v without assuming a unit vector exists, so dimension zero is included. This does not establish general nonlinear Cramer-Rao or any Brascamp-Lieb upper covariance.
